title: LLM Fine-tuning, Evaluation and Deployment Pipeline

nodes.label: ML engineer
nodes.summary: Defines the target behaviour, curates data, reviews evaluation results and approves releases.

nodes.label: Annotators
nodes.summary: Write demonstrations and rank model outputs. InstructGPT used a team of 40 contractors; Llama 3 collected human preference annotations over multi-turn dialogues.

nodes.label: End users
nodes.summary: Use the deployed model; their feedback and failures feed the next round.

nodes.label: Pretrained base model
nodes.summary: The starting checkpoint that is fine-tuned or adapted.

nodes.label: Data pipeline
nodes.summary: Curates and versions training data: rule-based cleaning, model-based pruning, topic, quality and difficulty scoring, semantic deduplication; keeps evaluation data separate.

nodes.label: Training jobs
nodes.summary: Runs fine-tuning on a GPU cluster: supervised fine-tuning, LoRA adapters, preference tuning and rejection sampling.

nodes.label: Supervised fine-tuning
nodes.summary: Fine-tunes on demonstrations of the desired behaviour; in Llama 3 every post-training round starts with SFT.

nodes.label: LoRA adapter training
nodes.summary: Freezes the base weights and trains small low-rank matrices: 10,000 times fewer trainable parameters and 3 times less GPU memory than full fine-tuning on GPT-3 175B in the paper.

nodes.label: Preference tuning (DPO or RLHF)
nodes.summary: Aligns the model to human preferences. InstructGPT used a reward model and PPO; DPO solves the problem with a simple classification loss and Llama 3 found it cheaper and better than PPO.

nodes.label: Rejection sampling
nodes.summary: Samples K outputs per prompt (typically 10 to 30) from the latest model and keeps the best by reward model, producing new training data.

nodes.label: Model and adapter registry
nodes.summary: Every model and adapter with its data version, config, metrics and approval state. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Evaluation gate
nodes.summary: Runs the suites on each candidate and decides whether it may ship: benchmarks, regression tests, judge-based quality, safety and cost.

nodes.label: Benchmarks and regression suite
nodes.summary: Target-task tests plus fixed tests of what the model did well before, compared with the production model. InstructGPT saw regressions on public datasets (alignment tax); contamination of test data is checked as in Llama 3.

nodes.label: LLM judge
nodes.summary: A strong model scores open-ended answers. Over 80% agreement with human preferences in MT-Bench tests, but position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases.

nodes.label: Safety evaluation
nodes.summary: Measures violation rate on adversarial prompts and false refusal rate on borderline prompts; Llama 3 optimises both.

nodes.label: Release gate
nodes.summary: Passes a candidate only if protected metrics do not regress against the production model beyond a threshold. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Canary router
nodes.summary: Sends a small share of traffic (after shadow testing) to the candidate, ramps up, and rolls back automatically on bad signals. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Serving (base + adapters)
nodes.summary: Shared base model with many LoRA adapters; S-LoRA keeps adapters in main memory, fetches those needed to the GPU, and batches requests across adapters with Unified Paging. See note 22.

nodes.label: Monitoring and feedback
nodes.summary: Tracks quality proxies, latency, cost, safety and drift; samples failures into the next round's data.

flows.name: From data to a released model

steps.caption: Annotators write demonstrations and rank outputs; the data pipeline cleans, scores and versions it.
The SFT checkpoint is tuned further on preference pairs.
The candidate model is registered with its data version and config.
The evaluation gate runs the target, regression, judge and safety suites on the candidate.
The gate approves it only if protected metrics do not regress.
A small canary share of traffic reaches it first.

flows.name: A candidate improves the target but regresses elsewhere (failure)

steps.caption: The candidate is better on the target task.
The regression suite shows it is worse on previously fixed cases or formats.
The gate blocks the release; the candidate stays unapproved and the data or training mix is revised.
A small share of users reaches the candidate.
Monitoring sees higher errors, latency or bad feedback on the candidate.
A rollback signal returns all traffic to the previous version.
The failing cases are sampled into the next round's data.
Each customer's adapter is registered after passing its own evaluation.
Adapters are stored in main memory on the serving fleet.
A request names its adapter; only the adapters used by running queries are fetched to GPU memory and batched together.
